translationRepairs: Qu Yuan followed Chu into exile and wrote his celebrated piece on the noble orange.
Qu Yuan was banished from Chu and wrote his celebrated piece on the noble orange.
靈均逐楚 means Lingjun/Qu Yuan was driven out from Chu; 'followed Chu into exile' reverses the agent/patient of 逐.
Lingjun followed Chu into exile and composed the chapter of auspicious calamity.
Lingjun was banished from Chu and composed the chapter of auspicious calamity.
Same 逐楚 error in the literal: banished from Chu, not following Chu into exile.

Under Emperor Xiaowen, literary culture flourished as never before: students were as numerous as ox hairs, but those who truly succeeded were as rare as unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is that not exactly the case?"

Under Emperor Suzong, literary culture flourished as never before: students were as numerous as ox hairs, but those who truly succeeded were as rare as unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is that not exactly the case?"
肅宗歷位 names Emperor Suzong; Xiaowen is 高祖 in the preceding sentence, not 肅宗.
Yuan Yue, whose style was Jingteng, came from Chen commandery and was the younger brother of Minister of Works Yuan Fan.
Yuan Yue, whose style was Jingteng, came from Chen commandery and was the younger brother of Minister Yuan Fan.
尚書翻 is Minister/Masters of Writing Yuan Fan; Minister of Works would be 司空.
Yuan Yue, style name Jingteng, was a man of Chen commandery and the younger brother of Minister of Works Yuan Fan.
Yuan Yue, style name Jingteng, was a man of Chen commandery and the younger brother of Minister Yuan Fan.
Literal likewise mistook 尚書 for Minister of Works; 'Minister Yuan Fan' matches the Chinese.
He was so submitted to by things.
Such was the deference things showed him.
為物所伏如此 is passive deference shown by others; the old literal is ungrammatical and opaque.
After the campaign he was appointed director of central arms in the left secretariat of the Ministry of Works, and soon died.
After the campaign he was appointed director of central arms in the left secretariat of the Masters of Writing, and soon died.
尚書左中兵郎中 belongs to the Masters of Writing, not the Ministry of Works (工部).
On return he was made Director of Central Arms in the Left Secretariat of the Ministry of Works and died.
On return he was made Director of Central Arms in the Left Secretariat of the Masters of Writing and died.
Same office-title error in the literal: 尚書 is Masters of Writing / Department of State Affairs.
Though the superior medicines of Lord Tong of the Divine Farmer sometimes helped;
Though Lord Tong's superior medicines sometimes took effect;
Source has only 桐君上藥; 'of the Divine Farmer' is an invented gloss absent from the Chinese.
Bomao was born after his brothers Gui and lived apart from his elder brother Jingrong.
Bomao had earlier been adopted as heir to his paternal uncle Zhonggui, and lived apart from his elder brother Jingrong.
出後其伯仲規 is the adoption formula for paternal uncle Zhonggui, not birth order after brothers Gui.
Bomao was born after his elder and younger brother Gui and lived separately from his elder brother Jingrong.
Bomao was first adopted as heir to his paternal uncle Zhonggui and lived separately from his elder brother Jingrong.
Literal same error: 先出後其伯仲規 marks adoption to uncle Zhonggui.
Shou was then at Jinyang and contributed his own piece on Bomao; its ten-character line read, "Facing the wind I think of Xu Xuan; over wine I think of Liu Gongrong."
Shou was then at Jinyang and contributed his own piece on Bomao; its ten-character line read, "Facing the wind I think of Xuandu; over wine I think of Gongrong."
Couplet quotes courtesy names 玄度 and 公榮; expanding them to Xu Xuan / Liu Gongrong invents wording not in the Chinese.
When Xiao Baoyin opened a field headquarters as Cavalry General-in-Chief to campaign in Guanzhong, he appointed Ziming Eastern Pavillion Libationer and entrusted him with official correspondence.
When Xiao Baoyin opened a field headquarters as Cavalry General-in-Chief to campaign in Guanzhong, he appointed Ziming Eastern Pavilion Libationer and entrusted him with official correspondence.
東閤祭酒 is Eastern Pavilion Libationer; 'Pavillion' is a spelling error in the office title.
When Xiao Baoyin served as Cavalry General-in-Chief with an open headquarters to campaign against Guanzhong, he made Ziming Eastern Pavillion Libationer and entrusted him with literary documents.
When Xiao Baoyin served as Cavalry General-in-Chief with an open headquarters to campaign against Guanzhong, he made Ziming Eastern Pavilion Libationer and entrusted him with literary documents.
Same Pavilion misspelling in the literal office title.

His grandfather Gongzhi had served as a clerk in the household of Liu Yikang's Prince of Pengcheng; fleeing turmoil he returned to the north, and the family settled at Yuanqu in Jiyin, thus becoming natives of that district.

His grandfather Gongzhi had served as a clerk in the household of Liu Yilong's Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang; fleeing turmoil he returned to the north, and the family settled at Yuanqu in Jiyin, thus becoming natives of that district.
劉義隆彭城王義康 names Liu Yilong then Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; 'Liu Yikang's Prince' fuses two persons.

His grandfather Gongzhi was a clerk in the household of Liu Yikang's Prince of Pengcheng; fleeing hardship he returned to the north, and the family settled in Yuanqu, Jiyin, thus becoming natives of that commandery and county.

His grandfather Gongzhi was a clerk in the household of Liu Yilong's Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang; fleeing hardship he returned to the north, and the family settled in Yuanqu, Jiyin, thus becoming natives of that commandery and county.
Literal repeats the same fused identification of 劉義隆 and 彭城王義康.
He was a lowly retainer of Prince Guangyang of Yuan Yuan; in the horse stables he taught the slave boys to write.
He was a lowly retainer of Prince Yuan of Guangyang; in the horse stables he taught the slave boys to write.
廣陽王淵 is Prince Yuan of Guangyang; 'Prince Guangyang of Yuan Yuan' garbles title and doubles the surname.

Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four directions and answered swiftly; facing Yuan alone he pondered and said: "They have Gentleman Wen of the Secretariat there—his literary talent is formidable."

Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four directions and answered swiftly; facing Yuan alone he pondered and said: "They have Gentleman Wen there—his literary talent is formidable."
Quoted speech has 溫郎中 only; 'of the Secretariat' is invented.
At the beginning of Jianyi, he was Southern Master of Guests Gentleman and compiled the Veritable Records.
At the beginning of Jianyi, he was Southern Master of Guests Gentleman and compiled the imperial diary.
修起居注 is compiling the imperial diary; Veritable Records would be 實錄.
Once he missed a day on duty; Prince Tianmu of Shangdang was then recording affairs of the Secretariat and was about to have him beaten; Zisheng fled.
Once he missed a day on duty; Prince Tianmu of Shangdang was then overseeing Secretariat affairs and was about to have him beaten; Zisheng fled.
錄尚書事 is the oversight post, not literal recording of Secretariat affairs.
He replied, "The sovereign, because Tiger Cage was lost, has been reduced to this plight.
He replied, "The sovereign, because Hulao was lost, has been reduced to this plight.
虎牢 is the fortress name Hulao; 'Tiger Cage' is a false calque.
Editorial note 8 They urged Zisheng to help draft the presentation speech.
They urged Zisheng to help draft the presentation speech.
推子昇合陳辭 has no editorial-note label; 'Editorial note 8' is invented English.
Editorial note 8 They pressed Zisheng to join in composing the formal address.
They pressed Zisheng to join in composing the formal address.
Literal likewise invents an editorial-note rubric absent from 推子昇合陳辭.

"Qu Yuan followed Chu into exile and composed the chapter on 'auspicious calamity'"—Commentary: The phrase "Jia huo" (auspicious calamity) has no known source. The Songs of Chu, "Ode to the Orange" in the Nine Pieces, reads: "O sovereign's noble tree, the orange has come to take root here."

"Lingjun was banished from Chu and composed the chapter on 'auspicious calamity'"—Commentary: The phrase "Jia huo" (auspicious calamity) has no known source. The Songs of Chu, "Ode to the Orange" in the Nine Pieces, reads: "O sovereign's noble tree, the orange has come to take root here."
Chinese begins 靈均逐楚; restoring Lingjun is right, but the proposal still keeps 'followed Chu into exile', which misreads 逐楚 as in r0001.
"In the third year of Yongxing"—Commentary: Yongxing was an era name of Tuoba Si (Emperor Daowu)
"In the third year of Yongxing"—Commentary: Yongxing was an era name of Tuoba Si (Emperor Mingyuan)
Commentary ties 永興 to 拓跋嗣; Tuoba Si is Emperor Mingyuan, whereas Daowu was Tuoba Gui.
A southern campaign against Jiang, Shu, and Chen Shuang's uprising—in the Comprehensive Records, volume 176, biography of Pei Bomao, "nan" (south) is written as "ji" (and).
A southern campaign against the Jiang-Shu rebel Chen Shuangchi—in the Comprehensive Records, volume 176, biography of Pei Bomao, "nan" (south) is written as "ji" (and).
南討絳蜀陳雙熾 names the Jiang-Shu rebel Chen Shuangchi; dropping 熾 and splitting Jiang/Shu invents a truncated name.
Southern campaign against Jiang and Shu, Chen Shuang's revolt—Comprehensive Records, scroll 176, Biography of Pei Bomao, reads "south" as "and".
Southern campaign against Jiang and Shu, Chen Shuangchi's revolt—Comprehensive Records, scroll 176, Biography of Pei Bomao, reads "south" as "and".
Literal must keep full personal name 陳雙熾; 'Chen Shuang' omits 熾.
When Emperor Xiaozong held the throne, refinement flourished greatly; learners were like ox-hairs, achievers like unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is it not so?"
When Emperor Suzong held the throne, refinement flourished greatly; learners were like ox-hairs, achievers like unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is it not so?"
肅宗 is Emperor Suzong; the literal's 'Xiaozong' invents a different temple name and must be corrected to match the Chinese and the already-fixed idiomatic line.
